title.en: Old Man River (drama by Dorothy Deming)

text.en: When a river rises beyond its banks, what matters most is courage, cooperation and being prepared.

Old Man River is a short play to be read aloud in scenes, with stage directions in brackets. Its characters include the teenage Marshall sisters, Amy and Betty, and their young neighbour Rose Field. The setting is a flood, and the play shows how people respond when rising water threatens their homes.
The unit links natural disasters such as cyclones, floods, earthquakes and tsunamis with human activities that harm nature, and asks us to think about precautions. A play teaches through dialogue, so pay attention to how each character speaks and acts under pressure.
Learn drama terms: scene, stage direction, dialogue, cast and enact. When you read aloud, follow the brackets for actions and tone. (The lesson is based on the textbook's introduction to the play and its warm-up tasks; read the full drama in your book.)
